questions.passage: Shel Silverstein’s poem “The Land of Happy” might be the most poignant critique of happiness. He describes the land of happy as a place where everyone is happy and everything is jolly. He ends his poem with: “What a bore.”
questions.prompt: How does Silverstein’s closing remark function in this account of his poem?
options: It reports a measured decline in a country’s happiness.
It shows that no one in the imagined land is happy.
It punctures the appeal of a place where everything is happy and jolly.
It recommends that readers move to the land described.
questions.promptZh: 这段介绍中，Silverstein 的结尾评论起什么作用？
optionsZh: 报告某国幸福度经测量下降。
表明想象中的地方没有一个人幸福。
削弱了那个人人幸福、处处欢乐之地的吸引力。
建议读者搬去所描写的地方。
analyses: A 诗歌评论没有国家测量数据。
B 人人幸福是诗中设定，bore 评价其乏味，不是否认设定。
C 最后的 What a bore 对前面的全然欢乐形成讽刺转折。
D 结尾批评乏味，并非迁居建议。

evidence.quote: He describes the land of happy as a place where everyone is happy and everything is jolly. He ends his poem with: “What a bore.”

questions.passage: Why so down on happiness? One common critique is that a happy life might be a selfish one. In reality, there is lots of evidence that suggests otherwise. For example, spending money on others as opposed to on oneself increases happiness.
questions.prompt: What does being 'down on happiness' mean in the rhetorical question?
questions.promptZh: 反问中 down on happiness 是什么意思？
options: Being physically below a written happiness score.
Having fewer opportunities to study happiness.
Being unable to feel any emotion.
Being critical or disapproving of happiness.
optionsZh: 位置处于书面幸福分数下方。
拥有较少研究幸福的机会。
无法感受任何情绪。
对幸福持批评或不赞同态度。
analyses: A down on 是态度表达，不是位置关系。
B 不是研究机会数量。
C 批评一个观念不等于无法感受情绪。
D 后文 One common critique 直接展开批评理由，支持此处 down on 的不赞同义；不把修辞问题当作临床诊断。

Happy people volunteer more than unhappy people.
Only unhappy people are allowed to volunteer.

两类人的志愿活动从无差异。
幸福的人比不幸福的人更多做志愿服务。
只允许不幸福的人做志愿服务。

B more than 与从无差异相反。

questions.passage: The novelist Donna Tartt suggested that it is “to make other people happy even at the expense of one’s own happiness”—in other words, what many scholars call a “meaningful life.” Meaning in life is typically defined by significance, purpose, and coherence. questions.prompt: How is significance first explained in this account of meaning in life?
options: A life matters to people beyond one’s family and friends.
A person receives public awards for every achievement.
A life has no obligations to strangers.
A person feels happy at every other person’s expense.
questions.promptZh: 这里首先怎样解释生命意义中的重要性？
optionsZh: 一个人的生活对家人朋友之外的人也有分量。
一个人每项成就都获得公众奖项。
一个人的生活对陌生人没有责任。
一个人靠牺牲所有他人的利益来幸福。

B matters 并未被定义为获奖。
C strangers 正是被纳入的对象。

evidence.quote: First, a meaningful life is a life that matters. It matters not just to one’s family members and friends, but also to strangers.

questions.passage: In contrast, a meaningless life is a life that does not make any difference in the world. Anthropologist David Graeber, in his book Bullshit Jobs: A Theory, argues that there are millions of people around the world who are toiling away their lives in meaningless jobs. He defines a bullshit job as a job that the person who is doing it can’t really justify the existence of that job.
questions.prompt: What distinguishes a “bullshit job” in Graeber’s definition here?
options: It requires strenuous physical labour.
It is any occupation held by millions of people.
It offers no opportunity to change employers.
Its holder cannot really justify why the job exists.
questions.promptZh: 在 Graeber 这里的定义中，“bullshit job”的区别性特征是什么？
optionsZh: 需要繁重体力劳动。
任何有数百万人从事的职业。
没有换雇主的机会。
从业者自己无法真正说明这份工作存在的理由。
analyses: A toiling away 描述辛劳耗日，并非这一定义的判据。
B millions 描述人数，不是职业类别的充分条件。
C 原文没有讨论换雇主机会。
D 定义明确落在从业者 can’t really justify the existence 上。

evidence.quote: He defines a bullshit job as a job that the person who is doing it can’t really justify the existence of that job.

vocabulary.meaning: 证明……有道理；为……提供充分理由
vocabulary.context: 这里指说明一份工作为何有必要存在
vocabulary.example: The manager was asked to justify the extra cost.

questions.translation: 相比之下，无意义的生活是对世界不产生任何影响的生活。人类学家 David Graeber 在《毫无意义的工作：一种理论》中认为，世界各地有数百万人正辛苦地把生命耗费在无意义的工作上。他把这种工作定义为：连从事它的人自己都无法真正说明其存在理由的工作。

questions.translation: 相比之下，无意义的生活是对世界不产生任何影响的生活。人类学家 David Graeber 在《毫无意义的工作：一种理论》中认为，世界各地有数百万人正辛苦地把生命耗费在无意义的工作上。他把这种工作定义为：连从事它的人自己都无法真正说明其存在理由的工作。

evidence.quote: In contrast, a meaningless life is a life that does not make any difference in the world.

questions.passage: In contrast, a meaningless life is a life that does not make any difference in the world. Anthropologist David Graeber, in his book Bullshit Jobs: A Theory, argues that there are millions of people around the world who are toiling away their lives in meaningless jobs. He defines a bullshit job as a job that the person who is doing it can’t really justify the existence of that job.
questions.prompt: Whose argument about millions of people in meaningless jobs is being reported?
questions.promptZh: 关于数百万人从事无意义工作的论点被归于谁？
options: Donna Tartt, presenting a definition of happiness.
David Graeber, in Bullshit Jobs: A Theory.
Michael Steger, reporting the informant survey.
Michelle Obama, addressing CUNY graduates.
optionsZh: 唐娜·塔特在定义幸福。
大卫·格雷伯，在《Bullshit Jobs: A Theory》中。
迈克尔·斯蒂格，在报告知情人调查。
米歇尔·奥巴马，向 CUNY 毕业生讲话。
analyses: A 塔特是前面关于他人幸福的引述来源，不是这条工作论点。
B Anthropologist David Graeber...argues 清楚给出人物、著作和论点归属。
C 斯蒂格属于后面的意义自报研究。
D 毕业演讲不是本句出处。不能把 argues 的转述性质抹成作者亲自统计证实。
